arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one original reward illustration for RevealLine's fictional spend-management / connected-business game theme. The player gradually uncovers the scenery, then sees the complete picture after winning. It is a game-world story, not an advertisement or product screenshot.
Format: exactly one full-bleed landscape 2:1 image, ideally 2048 by 1024 pixels. A single scene, not a contact sheet, infographic or UI mockup.
Style/medium: sophisticated modern pixel-art environmental illustration with nostalgic 16-bit adventure-game character. Deliberate square pixel clusters, crisp stepped silhouettes, restrained ordered dithering, clear broad masses and carefully chosen small discoveries. Rich directional illumination expressed as clustered colors. No photorealism, 3D render, vector gradients, soft painted blur or noisy CRT overlay.
Shared palette: deep ink navy and petrol shadows, clear cyan/teal structural accents, warm amber/apricot windows and copper/brass materials, selective cream and muted coral highlights. The palette is an original creative choice, not a claim to follow an official brand guide.
Concept: connected suppliers and businesses, thoughtful resource allocation, less waste and everyday savings made tangible through shipping, craft, planning and shared infrastructure. Any savings are fictional narrative ideas; no numerical promise or actual customer case.
Constraints: no readable text, letters, numerals, price tags, currency symbols, logos, brands, watermark or signature anywhere. No mascot, Navi character, Coupa logo or imitation of any identifiable brand asset. No dashboards, charts, HUD, menus, graph nodes, floating windows, crosshairs, baked gameplay trail or score. Any connections must be ordinary in-world infrastructure such as bridges, rail, cables or lamps, not graphic overlays. No copyrighted characters or copied game/film art. No people necessary. Opaque complete scenery to every edge.
Primary request: a beautiful working supply-network harbor at blue hour, viewed from a modest elevated dockside corner across calm water toward linked warehouses, workshops and a low town skyline. Near foreground, a sturdy unmarked cargo crate has been carefully packed with a small set of reusable containers, coiled cable and useful manufactured parts; a simple brass lifting hook and tidy bundled rope reveal human care without people. Beyond, short quay bridges and a compact rail line connect two distinct docks, a small freight boat, a crane and warm-lit warehouses. The same limited shapes and colors repeat across carefully organized cargo so shared supply feels connected and efficient rather than chaotic or wasteful. A sheltered store of surplus reusable crates suggests saved resources kept for the next journey. Selective cyan navigation lamps and amber window reflections guide the eye physically through the harbor; no floating network graphics or glowing painted arrows. Keep broad deep-blue water as calm visual space between detailed dock clusters. Welcoming, quietly industrious and optimistic; not a militarized port, giant dystopian megacity or corporate slide.

Primary request: an imaginative AI-assisted savings observatory overlooking a thriving compact city at early night. The viewpoint is inside a warm copper-and-dark-wood observatory with a huge open arched window. Its main foreground object is a wholly original physical planning instrument: a sculptural arrangement of small brass arms, rotating cyan glass lenses and carefully balanced counterweights above a tiny handmade model of several businesses. No face, mascot, letters, charts, screen or software UI. The device is an artistic metaphor for assistance and shared insight, not an actual Coupa product. Through the window, modest rooftops, workshops, a rail stop and a district greenhouse glow with warm windows; a few ordinary bridges and cable conduits connect them. A neat row of sealed resource containers near the instrument and fresh plants in the city show reserves preserved and value returned to everyday places. Composition contrasts the intimate still-life instrument against the broad navy city-and-sky view, with a clear cyan lens focal point and sparse amber constellations of windows. No laser grid, targeting beam, projected labels, floating data panels or generic dashboard. Quiet wonder and a sense of intelligent stewardship.

Primary request: a lively-looking but unoccupied procurement and maker-market workshop at warm midday, a welcoming covered arcade of small independent businesses opening onto a courtyard. A foreground oak workbench is organized with a simple brass balance, a few well-matched reusable parts, ceramic sample vessels, neatly folded fabric swatches and two plain shipping boxes nested efficiently. Show a repaired wooden container being returned to use, with simple hand tools laid aside, suggesting careful buying and less waste. Behind, distinct small workshops for ceramics, textiles and woodcraft share a common sheltered loading cart and matching reusable crate system, physically connected by the continuous arcade and a short courtyard path. Cyan-painted shutters and structural beams, cream plaster, brass/copper details and warm amber light unify the scene. Clear foreground silhouettes and broad quiet paving contrast with selected handcrafted details. No stalls with writing, blank poster-like panels, receipts, clipboards, price tags, money piles or diagrams; tell the procurement story entirely through useful goods, balanced choice and coordinated shared logistics. Original humane business fantasy rather than a museum, supermarket advertisement, corporate office or dashboard.
